segments.text: That seems like a big jump from one quiet Sunday afternoon. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ðæt simz laɪk ə bɪɡ dʒʌmp frʌm wʌn ˈkwaɪət ˈsʌnˌdeɪ ˌæftərˈnun ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Although I can understand the question.

segments.text: Earning money from something you enjoy can be wonderful.

segments.text: I just wish enjoying it were a complete answer, too.

segments.ipa: /tu ðæt ˈkwɛstʃən ˈpipəl æsk wɛn ðeɪ hir juv ˈstɑrtɪd ˈsʌmθɪŋ nu/

segments.text: I told a friend I was painting and she immediately suggested a store.
segments.ipa: /aɪ toʊld ə frɛnd aɪ wɑz ˈpeɪntɪŋ ənd ʃi ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli səˈdʒɛstɪd ə stɔr/

segments.text: Suddenly I was thinking about prices instead of colors.

segments.text: And you hadn't even decided whether the building was a kitchen or a bus stop.

segments.text: Then I looked at the painting differently.

segments.text: You began looking through somebody else's eyes.
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈɡæn ˈlʊkɪŋ θru ˈsʌmˌbɑdi ˈɛlsɪz aɪz/

segments.text: That's what surprised me.
segments.ipa: /ðæts wʌt sərˈpraɪzd mi/

segments.text: I wasn't proud of making a perfect picture.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈwɑzənt praʊd ʌv ˈmeɪkɪŋ ə pərˈfɛkt ˈpɪktʃər/

segments.text: I was happy I'd spent an hour noticing the light on my wall.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑz ˈhæpi aɪd spɛnt æn ˈaʊər ˈnoʊtɪsɪŋ ðə laɪt ɑn maɪ wɔl/

segments.text: That's a different kind of result.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈdɪfərənt kaɪnd ʌv rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: You paid attention to something familiar, and for a while, your mind wasn't running through a list. Right.
segments.ipa: /ju peɪd əˈtɛnʃən tu ˈsʌmθɪŋ fəˈmɪljər ənd fɔr ə waɪl jɔr maɪnd ˈwɑzənt ˈrʌnɪŋ θru ə lɪst raɪt/

segments.text: Do you have anything like that?
segments.ipa: /du ju hæv ˈɛniˌθɪŋ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: Something you enjoy that people keep trying to turn into your next big project? Bread.
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðæt ˈpipəl kip ˈtraɪɪŋ tu tɝn ˈɪntu jɔr nɛkst bɪɡ ˈprɑdʒɛkt brɛd/

segments.text: I started baking because I wanted to understand why my first loaf could probably hold a door open.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈstɑrtɪd ˈbeɪkɪŋ bɪˈkɔz aɪ ˈwɔntɪd tu ˌʌndərˈstænd waɪ maɪ fɝst loʊf kʊd ˈprɑbəˌbli hoʊld ə dɔr ˈoʊpən/

segments.text: The challenge was personal.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈtʃæləndʒ wɑz ˈpɝsɪnəl/

segments.text: A useful loaf just for the wrong reason.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈjusfəl loʊf dʒʌst fɔr ðə rɔŋ ˈrizən/

segments.text: Did people start placing orders when your bread finally became something you could eat? Almost immediately.
segments.ipa: /dɪd ˈpipəl stɑrt ˈpleɪsɪŋ ˈɔrdərz wɛn jɔr brɛd ˈfaɪnəli bɪˈkeɪm ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju kʊd it ˈɔlˌmoʊst ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli/

segments.text: I took some to a family dinner, and my cousin said, "You should sell these.
segments.ipa: /aɪ tʊk sʌm tu ə ˈfæməli ˈdɪnər ənd maɪ ˈkʌzən sɛd ju ʃʊd sɛl ðiz/

segments.text: People would pay good money."
segments.ipa: /ˈpipəl wʊd peɪ ɡʊd ˈmʌni/

segments.text: That sounds kind on the surface.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz kaɪnd ɑn ðə ˈsɝfəs/

segments.text: He liked your bread, but did it make you feel you had to take the next step? A little.
segments.ipa: /hi laɪkt jɔr brɛd bʌt dɪd ɪt meɪk ju fil ju hæd tu teɪk ðə nɛkst stɛp ə ˈlɪtəl/

segments.text: I thought, "Am I wasting a chance?"
segments.ipa: /aɪ θɔt æm aɪ ˈweɪstɪŋ ə tʃæns/

segments.text: Then I imagined baking 20 loaves before work and answering messages about late deliveries.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ ˌɪˈmædʒənd ˈbeɪkɪŋ loʊvz bɪˈfɔr wɝk ənd ˈænsərɪŋ ˈmɛsədʒəz əˈbaʊt leɪt dɪˈlɪvəriz/

segments.text: And the activity you chose for a quiet evening suddenly needed a calendar, a price list,
segments.ipa: /ənd ðə ækˈtɪvəti ju tʃoʊz fɔr ə ˈkwaɪət ˈivnɪŋ ˈsʌdənli ˈnidəd ə ˈkæləndər ə praɪs lɪst/

segments.text: and customers waiting for you. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈkʌstəmərz ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ju ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: I enjoy trying again when the bread goes wrong.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈtraɪɪŋ əˈɡɛn wɛn ðə brɛd ɡoʊz rɔŋ/

segments.text: I wouldn't enjoy telling 20 hungry people that today's lesson was patience.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈwʊdənt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈtɛlɪŋ ˈhʌŋɡri ˈpipəl ðæt təˈdeɪz ˈlɛsən wɑz ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: That's an important difference.
segments.ipa: /ðæts æn ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt ˈdɪfərəns/

segments.text: When you're making something for yourself, a mistake can stay small.
segments.ipa: /wɛn jʊr ˈmeɪkɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ fɔr jərˈsɛlf ə mɪˈsteɪk kæn steɪ smɔl/

segments.text: When someone's paid you, there's another responsibility.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ˈsʌmˌwʌnz peɪd ju ðɛrz əˈnʌðər riˌspɑnsəˈbɪləti/

segments.text: Which doesn't mean selling bread is a bad idea.
segments.ipa: /wɪtʃ ˈdʌzənt min ˈsɛlɪŋ brɛd ɪz ə bæd aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: It means enjoying baking and enjoying running a baking business aren't the same thing.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪɪŋ ˈbeɪkɪŋ ənd ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪɪŋ ˈrʌnɪŋ ə ˈbeɪkɪŋ ˈbɪznəs ˈɑrənt ðə seɪm θɪŋ/

segments.text: Yes, and it's okay to discover you want one without the other.
segments.ipa: /jɛs ənd ɪts ˌoʊˈkeɪ tu dɪˈskʌvər ju wɑnt wʌn wɪˈθaʊt ðə ˈʌðər/

segments.text: A hobby is something you do because you enjoy doing it.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhɑbi ɪz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju du bɪˈkɔz ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈduɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: Like gardening, drawing, fixing old radios, or playing basketball with friends.
segments.ipa: /laɪk ˈɡɑrdənɪŋ ˈdrɔɪŋ ˈfɪksɪŋ oʊld ˈreɪdiˌoʊz ɔr ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈbæskətˌbɔl wɪð frɛndz/

segments.text: It doesn't have to produce something you can put on a shelf.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈdʌzənt hæv tu prəˈdus ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju kæn pʊt ɑn ə ʃɛlf/

segments.text: I'm glad you mentioned basketball.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ɡlæd ju ˈmɛnʃənd ˈbæskətˌbɔl/

segments.text: Nobody usually asks, "When will your Saturday game start making money?"
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi ˈjuʒəwəli æsks wɛn wɪl jɔr ˈsætərdi ɡeɪm stɑrt ˈmeɪkɪŋ ˈmʌni/

segments.text: But someone learns to sew, and suddenly there's a business plan.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈsʌmˌwʌn lɝnz tu soʊ ənd ˈsʌdənli ðɛrz ə ˈbɪznəs plæn/

segments.text: Maybe because we can imagine buying a shirt more easily than buying somebody's Saturday game.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi bɪˈkɔz wi kæn ˌɪˈmædʒən ˈbaɪɪŋ ə ʃɝt mɔr ˈizəli ðæn ˈbaɪɪŋ ˈsʌmˌbɑdiz ˈsætərdi ɡeɪm/

segments.text: We see the object and forget the experience. That's true.
segments.ipa: /wi si ðə ˈɑbdʒɛkt ənd fərˈɡɛt ðə ɪkˈspɪriəns ðæts tru/

segments.text: And sometimes we do it to ourselves.
segments.ipa: /ənd səmˈtaɪmz wi du ɪt tu aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: I used to play guitar after dinner.
segments.ipa: /aɪ juzd tu pleɪ ɡɪˈtɑr ˈæftər ˈdɪnər/

segments.text: Then I started thinking I should record songs, post them, and show some progress.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ ˈstɑrtɪd ˈθɪŋkɪŋ aɪ ʃʊd rəˈkɔrd sɔŋz poʊst ðɛm ənd ʃoʊ sʌm ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: Did recording help you enjoy playing, or did it make you listen for every little mistake before you'd even finished a song?
segments.ipa: /dɪd rəˈkɔrdɪŋ hɛlp ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈpleɪɪŋ ɔr dɪd ɪt meɪk ju ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈɛvəri ˈlɪtəl mɪˈsteɪk bɪˈfɔr jud ˈivɪn ˈfɪnɪʃt ə sɔŋ/

segments.text: The second one.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈsɛkənd wʌn/

segments.text: I kept starting over.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kɛpt ˈstɑrtɪŋ ˈoʊvər/

segments.text: One evening I spent more time moving my phone around than touching the guitar.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈivnɪŋ aɪ spɛnt mɔr taɪm ˈmuvɪŋ maɪ foʊn ərˈaʊnd ðæn ˈtʌtʃɪŋ ðə ɡɪˈtɑr/

segments.text: That sounds familiar.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz fəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: With my painting, I almost cleaned the whole table to take a picture.
segments.ipa: /wɪð maɪ ˈpeɪntɪŋ aɪ ˈɔlˌmoʊst klind ðə hoʊl ˈteɪbəl tu teɪk ə ˈpɪktʃər/

segments.text: Then I remembered nobody was waiting for a picture.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ rɪˈmɛmbərd ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi wɑz ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ə ˈpɪktʃər/

segments.text: So you left the table alone, paint, old mug, sad bus stop, and all?

segments.text: That sounds like a fairly honest Sunday afternoon.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz laɪk ə ˈfɛrli ˈɑnəst ˈsʌnˌdeɪ ˌæftərˈnun/

segments.text: I did, and I stayed there longer.

segments.text: Without a photo to prepare, I noticed I wanted to paint the little plant beside the window. That's interesting.
segments.ipa: /wɪˈθaʊt ə ˈfoʊˌtoʊ tu priˈpɛr aɪ ˈnoʊtəst aɪ ˈwɔntɪd tu peɪnt ðə ˈlɪtəl plænt bɪˈsaɪd ðə ˈwɪndoʊ ðæts ˈɪntrəstɪŋ/

segments.text: Taking away the need to show a result gave you another idea.

segments.text: The activity itself was enough to keep you there.

segments.text: For that afternoon, yes.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ðæt ˌæftərˈnun jɛs/

segments.text: But I know just enjoy yourself can sound easy when someone else is worried about bills or working two jobs. It can.

segments.text: If money's tight, an extra skill might matter a lot.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈmʌniz taɪt æn ˈɛkstrə skɪl maɪt ˈmætər ə lɑt/

segments.text: We shouldn't make anyone feel bad for needing to earn more. Absolutely.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈʃʊdənt meɪk ˈɛniˌwʌn fil bæd fɔr ˈnidɪŋ tu ɝn mɔr ˌæbsəˈlutli/

segments.text: I don't want to turn free time into another thing people can do wrong.
segments.ipa: /aɪ doʊnt wɑnt tu tɝn fri taɪm ˈɪntu əˈnʌðər θɪŋ ˈpipəl kæn du rɔŋ/

segments.text: Some weeks finding 10 quiet minutes is already difficult.

segments.text: Then maybe we need to look at what those 10 minutes can realistically hold,
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈmeɪbi wi nid tu lʊk æt wʌt ðoʊz ˈmɪnəts kæn ˌriəˈlɪstɪkli hoʊld/

segments.text: especially when everyone around us has suggestions for them.
segments.ipa: /əˈspɛʃli wɛn ˈɛvriˌwʌn ərˈaʊnd ʌs hæz səˈdʒɛstʃənz fɔr ðɛm/

segments.text: Those suggestions can make 10 minutes feel crowded before you've even started.
segments.ipa: /ðoʊz səˈdʒɛstʃənz kæn meɪk ˈmɪnəts fil ˈkraʊdəd bɪˈfɔr juv ˈivɪn ˈstɑrtɪd/

segments.text: My sister's 32, and she recently told me something like that.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstərz ənd ʃi ˈrisəntli toʊld mi ˈsʌmθɪŋ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: Was she trying to find a hobby, or trying to find room for one she already had?
segments.ipa: /wɑz ʃi ˈtraɪɪŋ tu faɪnd ə ˈhɑbi ɔr ˈtraɪɪŋ tu faɪnd rum fɔr wʌn ʃi ɔlˈrɛdi hæd/

segments.text: Those are quite different problems.
segments.ipa: /ðoʊz ɑr kwaɪt ˈdɪfərənt ˈprɑbləmz/

segments.text: Room for one.
segments.ipa: /rum fɔr wʌn/

segments.text: She likes sewing, but between work and looking after her little girl, the machine usually stays in a cupboard.
segments.ipa: /ʃi laɪks ˈsoʊɪŋ bʌt bɪˈtwin wɝk ənd ˈlʊkɪŋ ˈæftər hɝ ˈlɪtəl ɡɝl ðə məˈʃin ˈjuʒəwəli steɪz ɪn ə ˈkʌbərd/

segments.text: Getting it out probably feels like the beginning of a whole project.
segments.ipa: /ˈɡɛtɪŋ ɪt aʊt ˈprɑbəˌbli filz laɪk ðə bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ ʌv ə hoʊl ˈprɑdʒɛkt/

segments.text: Then putting everything away becomes another job at the end. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈpʌtɪŋ ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ əˈweɪ bɪˈkʌmz əˈnʌðər dʒɑb æt ðə ɛnd ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: So, she stopped planning big projects.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ʃi stɑpt ˈplænɪŋ bɪɡ ˈprɑdʒɛkts/

segments.text: One evening, she fixed the pocket on her daughter's jacket using a little piece of bright yellow fabric.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈivnɪŋ ʃi fɪkst ðə ˈpɑkət ɑn hɝ ˈdɔtərz ˈdʒækət ˈjuzɪŋ ə ˈlɪtəl pis ʌv braɪt ˈjɛloʊ ˈfæbrɪk/

segments.text: That's small enough to finish, and it makes the jacket personal.
segments.ipa: /ðæts smɔl ɪˈnʌf tu ˈfɪnɪʃ ənd ɪt meɪks ðə ˈdʒækət ˈpɝsɪnəl/

segments.text: Did her daughter like having a pocket that looked different?
segments.ipa: /dɪd hɝ ˈdɔtər laɪk ˈhævɪŋ ə ˈpɑkət ðæt lʊkt ˈdɪfərənt/

segments.text: She loved it.
segments.ipa: /ʃi lʌvd ɪt/

segments.text: She calls it her sunshine pocket.
segments.ipa: /ʃi kɔlz ɪt hɝ ˈsʌnˌʃaɪn ˈpɑkət/

segments.text: My sister said that was the first time all week she'd made something slowly.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər sɛd ðæt wɑz ðə fɝst taɪm ɔl wik ʃid meɪd ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: I like that detail. Slowly.
segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt dɪˈteɪl ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: Her day probably asks her to move quickly everywhere else.
segments.ipa: /hɝ deɪ ˈprɑbəˌbli æsks hɝ tu muv ˈkwɪkli ˈɛvriˌwɛr ɛls/

segments.text: Sewing gave her a different speed for a while. It did.
segments.ipa: /ˈsoʊɪŋ ɡeɪv hɝ ə ˈdɪfərənt spid fɔr ə waɪl ɪt dɪd/

segments.text: Then someone saw the jacket and asked if she'd make 10 more.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈsʌmˌwʌn sɔ ðə ˈdʒækət ənd æskt ɪf ʃid meɪk mɔr/

segments.text: She said she suddenly wanted to hide the sewing machine again.
segments.ipa: /ʃi sɛd ʃi ˈsʌdənli ˈwɔntɪd tu haɪd ðə ˈsoʊɪŋ məˈʃin əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: 10 jackets would take away the little space she just found.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒækɪts wʊd teɪk əˈweɪ ðə ˈlɪtəl speɪs ʃi dʒʌst faʊnd/

segments.text: Did she feel comfortable saying she didn't want the order?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ʃi fil ˈkʌmfərtəbəl ˈseɪɪŋ ʃi ˈdɪdənt wɑnt ðə ˈɔrdər/

segments.text: Not at first.
segments.ipa: /nɑt æt fɝst/

segments.text: She started explaining how busy she was, but really she didn't want to prove she had a good enough excuse.
segments.ipa: /ʃi ˈstɑrtɪd ɪkˈspleɪnɪŋ haʊ ˈbɪzi ʃi wɑz bʌt ˈrɪli ʃi ˈdɪdənt wɑnt tu pruv ʃi hæd ə ɡʊd ɪˈnʌf ɪkskˈjus/

segments.text: That's where simple English can help.
segments.ipa: /ðæts wɛr ˈsɪmpəl ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ kæn hɛlp/

segments.text: You can appreciate a kind offer without giving somebody a long report about your whole life.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn əˈpriʃiˌeɪt ə kaɪnd ˈɔfər wɪˈθaʊt ˈɡɪvɪŋ ˈsʌmˌbɑdi ə lɔŋ riˈpɔrt əˈbaʊt jɔr hoʊl laɪf/

segments.text: Let's show what that sounds like.
segments.ipa: /lɛts ʃoʊ wʌt ðæt saʊndz laɪk/

segments.text: I'll be the person who sees the jacket.
segments.ipa: /aɪl bi ðə ˈpɝsən hu siz ðə ˈdʒækət/

segments.text: You answer as someone who wants to keep sewing for fun.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈænsər æz ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu wɑnts tu kip ˈsoʊɪŋ fɔr fʌn/

segments.text: Okay, here's our short example.
segments.ipa: /ˌoʊˈkeɪ hɪrz ˈaʊər ʃɔrt ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: I'm by the door with the jacket, and you've just noticed the pocket.
segments.ipa: /aɪm baɪ ðə dɔr wɪð ðə ˈdʒækət ənd juv dʒʌst ˈnoʊtəst ðə ˈpɑkət/

segments.text: What do you say?
segments.ipa: /wʌt du ju seɪ/

segments.text: That pocket looks great.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ˈpɑkət lʊks ɡreɪt/

segments.text: My friend runs a little store.
segments.ipa: /maɪ frɛnd rʌnz ə ˈlɪtəl stɔr/

segments.text: Would you like me to ask if she'd sell some jackets for you?
segments.ipa: /wʊd ju laɪk mi tu æsk ɪf ʃid sɛl sʌm ˈdʒækɪts fɔr ju/

segments.text: That's really kind of you.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈrɪli kaɪnd ʌv ju/

segments.text: I'm keeping sewing as a hobby for now, but I'm glad you like what I made.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈkipɪŋ ˈsoʊɪŋ æz ə ˈhɑbi fɔr naʊ bʌt aɪm ɡlæd ju laɪk wʌt aɪ meɪd/

segments.text: That sounds warm and clear, and that's the end of our example.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz wɔrm ənd klɪr ənd ðæts ðə ɛnd ʌv ˈaʊər ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: You thanked me without saying yes to something you didn't want. Right.
segments.ipa: /ju θæŋkt mi wɪˈθaʊt ˈseɪɪŋ jɛs tu ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ˈdɪdənt wɑnt raɪt/

segments.text: I'm keeping it as a hobby for now leaves the choice with you.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈkipɪŋ ɪt æz ə ˈhɑbi fɔr naʊ livz ðə tʃɔɪs wɪð ju/

segments.text: You haven't promised to change your mind later.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈhævənt ˈprɑməst tu tʃeɪndʒ jɔr maɪnd ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: And if you want an even shorter answer, you can say, I do it for fun.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ju wɑnt æn ˈivɪn ˈʃɔrtər ˈænsər ju kæn seɪ aɪ du ɪt fɔr fʌn/

segments.text: That's a full reason even if the words are simple. Right.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə fʊl ˈrizən ˈivɪn ɪf ðə wɝdz ɑr ˈsɪmpəl raɪt/

segments.text: But what if somebody says you're wasting your talent?
segments.ipa: /bʌt wʌt ɪf ˈsʌmˌbɑdi sɛz jʊr ˈweɪstɪŋ jɔr ˈtælənt/

segments.text: That can be a harder to hear when there's someone you care about.
segments.ipa: /ðæt kæn bi ə ˈhɑrdər tu hir wɛn ðɛrz ˈsʌmˌwʌn ju kɛr əˈbaʊt/

segments.text: I'd probably say, I understand what you mean.
segments.ipa: /aɪd ˈprɑbəˌbli seɪ aɪ ˌʌndərˈstænd wʌt ju min/

segments.text: I just enjoy doing it this way.
segments.ipa: /aɪ dʒʌst ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈduɪŋ ɪt ðɪs weɪ/

segments.text: I don't need to win an argument about my talent. That helps.
segments.ipa: /aɪ doʊnt nid tu wɪn æn ˈɑrɡjəmənt əˈbaʊt maɪ ˈtælənt ðæt hɛlps/

segments.text: Sometimes the person is trying to encourage you, but they're using the only kind of success they know how to measure.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ðə ˈpɝsən ɪz ˈtraɪɪŋ tu ɛnˈkɝɪdʒ ju bʌt ðɛr ˈjuzɪŋ ðə ˈoʊnli kaɪnd ʌv səkˈsɛs ðeɪ noʊ haʊ tu ˈmɛʒər/

segments.text: Yes, and we can give encouragement differently.
segments.ipa: /jɛs ənd wi kæn ɡɪv ɛnˈkɝɪdʒmənt ˈdɪfrəntli/

segments.text: Instead of asking what someone's going to sell, ask, what do you enjoy about making it?
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈæskɪŋ wʌt ˈsʌmˌwʌnz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu sɛl æsk wʌt du ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ əˈbaʊt ˈmeɪkɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: Or will you show me how you did that?
segments.ipa: /ɔr wɪl ju ʃoʊ mi haʊ ju dɪd ðæt/

segments.text: I'd love somebody to ask about my bread without ordering 12 loaves for Saturday.
segments.ipa: /aɪd lʌv ˈsʌmˌbɑdi tu æsk əˈbaʊt maɪ brɛd wɪˈθaʊt ˈɔrdərɪŋ loʊvz fɔr ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: I can ask about the bread, but I may still want a slice.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn æsk əˈbaʊt ðə brɛd bʌt aɪ meɪ stɪl wɑnt ə slaɪs/

segments.text: Interest and hunger can at the same time. That's fair.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪntrəst ənd ˈhʌŋɡər kæn æt ðə seɪm taɪm ðæts fɛr/

segments.text: And giving someone a slice feels different from taking an order.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈɡɪvɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn ə slaɪs filz ˈdɪfərənt frʌm ˈteɪkɪŋ æn ˈɔrdər/

segments.text: I get to choose when and how much.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ɡɛt tu tʃuz wɛn ənd haʊ mʌtʃ/

segments.text: That choice matters with gifts, too.
segments.ipa: /ðæt tʃɔɪs ˈmætərz wɪð ɡɪfts tu/

segments.text: My sister likes making one special thing for someone.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər laɪks ˈmeɪkɪŋ wʌn ˈspɛʃəl θɪŋ fɔr ˈsʌmˌwʌn/

segments.text: She doesn't want every birthday to become a deadline.
segments.ipa: /ʃi ˈdʌzənt wɑnt ˈɛvəri ˈbɝθˌdeɪ tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈdɛdˌlaɪn/

segments.text: So even a hobby that makes no money can start feeling like a job if everybody expects you to provide something regularly.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˈivɪn ə ˈhɑbi ðæt meɪks noʊ ˈmʌni kæn stɑrt ˈfilɪŋ laɪk ə dʒɑb ɪf ˈɛvriˌbɑdi ɪkˈspɛkts ju tu prəˈvaɪd ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈrɛɡjələrli/

segments.text: Yes, especially if you always say yes.
segments.ipa: /jɛs əˈspɛʃli ɪf ju ˈɔlˌweɪz seɪ jɛs/

segments.text: You might need to say, I'd love to help, but I can't make that this time.
segments.ipa: /ju maɪt nid tu seɪ aɪd lʌv tu hɛlp bʌt aɪ kænt meɪk ðæt ðɪs taɪm/

segments.text: That's useful beyond hobbies, actually.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈjusfəl bɪˈɑnd ˈhɑbiz ˈækˌtʃuəli/

segments.text: And if these little conversations help you, subscribe to Mr.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ðiz ˈlɪtəl ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz hɛlp ju səbˈskraɪb tu ˈmɪstər/

segments.text: English channel and give this episode a like.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl ənd ɡɪv ðɪs ˈɛpəˌsoʊd ə laɪk/

segments.text: And tell us in the comments what you enjoy doing just for yourself.
segments.ipa: /ənd tɛl ʌs ɪn ðə ˈkɑmɛnts wʌt ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈduɪŋ dʒʌst fɔr jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: You can practice the sentence, I do it for fun.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈpræktəs ðə ˈsɛntəns aɪ du ɪt fɔr fʌn/

segments.text: I'd love to read those answers, especially from someone who's just beginning.
segments.ipa: /aɪd lʌv tu rɛd ðoʊz ˈænsərz əˈspɛʃli frʌm ˈsʌmˌwʌn huz dʒʌst bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ/

segments.text: People often think they need to be good before they they call something a hobby.
segments.ipa: /ˈpipəl ˈɔfən θɪŋk ðeɪ nid tu bi ɡʊd bɪˈfɔr ðeɪ ðeɪ kɔl ˈsʌmθɪŋ ə ˈhɑbi/

segments.text: I'm glad you said that.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ɡlæd ju sɛd ðæt/

segments.text: A student once told me she couldn't say she liked drawing because her pictures didn't look real enough.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈstudənt wʌns toʊld mi ʃi ˈkʊdənt seɪ ʃi laɪkt ˈdrɔɪŋ bɪˈkɔz hɝ ˈpɪktʃərz ˈdɪdənt lʊk ril ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: But, I like drawing describes what she enjoys.
segments.ipa: /bʌt aɪ laɪk ˈdrɔɪŋ dɪˈskraɪbz wʌt ʃi ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪz/

segments.text: It doesn't claim she's ready to draw every person in the room perfectly. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈdʌzənt kleɪm ʃiz ˈrɛdi tu drɔ ˈɛvəri ˈpɝsən ɪn ðə rum ˈpɝfəktli ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: I'm still learning is another helpful phrase.
segments.ipa: /aɪm stɪl ˈlɝnɪŋ ɪz əˈnʌðər ˈhɛlpfəl freɪz/

segments.text: You can say, "I like drawing and I'm still learning."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪ laɪk ˈdrɔɪŋ ənd aɪm stɪl ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Both things can be true.
segments.ipa: /boʊθ θɪŋz kæn bi tru/

segments.text: That also makes it easier to talk about an activity you've put down for a while.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ˈɔlsoʊ meɪks ɪt ˈiziər tu tɔk əˈbaʊt æn ækˈtɪvəti juv pʊt daʊn fɔr ə waɪl/

segments.text: "I'm getting back into it" means you're starting again.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡɛtɪŋ bæk ˈɪntu ɪt minz jʊr ˈstɑrtɪŋ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Like your guitar.
segments.ipa: /laɪk jɔr ɡɪˈtɑr/

segments.text: You could say, "I'm getting back into playing after dinner."
segments.ipa: /ju kʊd seɪ aɪm ˈɡɛtɪŋ bæk ˈɪntu ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈæftər ˈdɪnər/

segments.text: Nobody needs a new song, a video, or a public announcement.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi nidz ə nu sɔŋ ə ˈvɪdioʊ ɔr ə ˈpʌblɪk əˈnaʊnsmənt/

segments.text: I might actually try that tonight, but I know myself I'll open a lesson online and see someone playing beautifully after 3 weeks.
segments.ipa: /aɪ maɪt ˈækˌtʃuəli traɪ ðæt təˈnaɪt bʌt aɪ noʊ ˌmaɪˈsɛlf aɪl ˈoʊpən ə ˈlɛsən ˈɔnˌlaɪn ənd si ˈsʌmˌwʌn ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈbjutəfli ˈæftər wiks/

segments.text: Then maybe choose the lesson before you pick up the guitar.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈmeɪbi tʃuz ðə ˈlɛsən bɪˈfɔr ju pɪk ʌp ðə ɡɪˈtɑr/

segments.text: Go straight to what you need instead of spending your whole evening comparing. That's practical.
segments.ipa: /ɡoʊ streɪt tu wʌt ju nid ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈspɛndɪŋ jɔr hoʊl ˈivnɪŋ kəmˈpɛrɪŋ ðæts ˈpræktəkəl/

segments.text: I don't need to turn the internet off forever.
segments.ipa: /aɪ doʊnt nid tu tɝn ðə ˈɪntərˌnɛt ɔf fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: I just need to stop letting the next video choose what my evening should become.
segments.ipa: /aɪ dʒʌst nid tu stɑp ˈlɛtɪŋ ðə nɛkst ˈvɪdioʊ tʃuz wʌt maɪ ˈivnɪŋ ʃʊd bɪˈkʌm/

segments.text: And you can enjoy learning a difficult song if that's what you want.
segments.ipa: /ənd ju kæn ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈlɝnɪŋ ə ˈdɪfəkəlt sɔŋ ɪf ðæts wʌt ju wɑnt/

segments.text: Keeping something for fun doesn't mean you have to stay at the same level. True.
segments.ipa: /ˈkipɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ fɔr fʌn ˈdʌzənt min ju hæv tu steɪ æt ðə seɪm ˈlɛvəl tru/

segments.text: I used to learn songs because my dad would sing along.
segments.ipa: /aɪ juzd tu lɝn sɔŋz bɪˈkɔz maɪ dæd wʊd sɪŋ əˈlɔŋ/

segments.text: I'd forgotten that until we started talking about the guitar today.
segments.ipa: /aɪd fərˈɡɑtən ðæt ənˈtɪl wi ˈstɑrtɪd ˈtɔkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə ɡɪˈtɑr təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: That's a lovely reason to learn a song.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈlʌvli ˈrizən tu lɝn ə sɔŋ/

segments.text: Did your dad care if you played every note correctly or was he happy to sing with you?
segments.ipa: /dɪd jɔr dæd kɛr ɪf ju pleɪd ˈɛvəri noʊt kərˈɛktli ɔr wɑz hi ˈhæpi tu sɪŋ wɪð ju/

segments.text: He'd notice when I missed one, mostly because he'd come in singing at completely the wrong time.
segments.ipa: /hid ˈnoʊtəs wɛn aɪ mɪst wʌn ˈmoʊstli bɪˈkɔz hid kʌm ɪn ˈsɪŋɪŋ æt kəmˈplitli ðə rɔŋ taɪm/

segments.text: But, he'd keep going anyway.
segments.ipa: /bʌt hid kip ˈɡoʊɪŋ ˈɛniˌweɪ/

segments.text: So, you were both trying to find each other in the song.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ju wɝ boʊθ ˈtraɪɪŋ tu faɪnd itʃ ˈʌðər ɪn ðə sɔŋ/

segments.text: That sounds more enjoyable than playing perfectly for a camera. It was.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz mɔr ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪəbəl ðæn ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈpɝfəktli fɔr ə ˈkæmərə ɪt wɑz/

segments.text: He lives farther away now and we mostly talk about appointments, the weather, and things around the house that need fixing.
segments.ipa: /hi lɪvz ˈfɑrðər əˈweɪ naʊ ənd wi ˈmoʊstli tɔk əˈbaʊt əˈpɔɪntmənts ðə ˈwɛðər ənd θɪŋz ərˈaʊnd ðə haʊs ðæt nid ˈfɪksɪŋ/

segments.text: The practical things can fill a whole call.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəkəl θɪŋz kæn fɪl ə hoʊl kɔl/

segments.text: Could you ask what he'd like to sing next time you visit instead of waiting for it to happen? I could.
segments.ipa: /kʊd ju æsk wʌt hid laɪk tu sɪŋ nɛkst taɪm ju ˈvɪzɪt ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ɪt tu ˈhæpən aɪ kʊd/

segments.text: He'd probably name something I don't know.
segments.ipa: /hid ˈprɑbəˌbli neɪm ˈsʌmθɪŋ aɪ doʊnt noʊ/

segments.text: Then he'd send me three different versions and call to ask which one I'd chosen.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn hid sɛnd mi θri ˈdɪfərənt ˈvɝʒənz ənd kɔl tu æsk wɪtʃ wʌn aɪd ˈtʃoʊzən/

segments.text: And your guitar would give you something new to talk about before you even got there.
segments.ipa: /ənd jɔr ɡɪˈtɑr wʊd ɡɪv ju ˈsʌmθɪŋ nu tu tɔk əˈbaʊt bɪˈfɔr ju ˈivɪn ɡɑt ðɛr/

segments.text: That's a pretty good use of an evening.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈprɪti ɡʊd jus ʌv æn ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: Yeah, I think I've been waiting to have more free time before I picked it up again,
segments.ipa: /jæ aɪ θɪŋk aɪv bɪn ˈweɪtɪŋ tu hæv mɔr fri taɪm bɪˈfɔr aɪ pɪkt ɪt ʌp əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: but there's always another task ready for that time.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðɛrz ˈɔlˌweɪz əˈnʌðər tæsk ˈrɛdi fɔr ðæt taɪm/

segments.text: There usually is.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ˈjuʒəwəli ɪz/

segments.text: That's why I don't think when everything's done works very well as a plan.
segments.ipa: /ðæts waɪ aɪ doʊnt θɪŋk wɛn ˈɛvriˌθɪŋz dʌn wɝks ˈvɛri wɛl æz ə plæn/

segments.text: For many people, everything is never done.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈmɛni ˈpipəl ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ ɪz ˈnɛvər dʌn/

segments.text: So how do you make room without adding another strict rule?
segments.ipa: /soʊ haʊ du ju meɪk rum wɪˈθaʊt ˈædɪŋ əˈnʌðər strɪkt rul/

segments.text: I don't want someone listening to feel they failed because they didn't paint this week.
segments.ipa: /aɪ doʊnt wɑnt ˈsʌmˌwʌn ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu fil ðeɪ feɪld bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ ˈdɪdənt peɪnt ðɪs wik/

segments.text: Maybe start by noticing one realistic opening.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi stɑrt baɪ ˈnoʊtɪsɪŋ wʌn ˌriəˈlɪstɪk ˈoʊpənɪŋ/

segments.text: After dinner on Thursday, 10 minutes before a show, or a little time while the laundry runs.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈdɪnər ɑn ˈθɝzˌdeɪ ˈmɪnəts bɪˈfɔr ə ʃoʊ ɔr ə ˈlɪtəl taɪm waɪl ðə ˈlɔndri rʌnz/

segments.text: And choose something that fits the opening rather than buying everything for a big new activity.
segments.ipa: /ənd tʃuz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt fɪts ðə ˈoʊpənɪŋ ˈræðər ðæn ˈbaɪɪŋ ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ fɔr ə bɪɡ nu ækˈtɪvəti/

segments.text: The buying can become its own distraction. Oh, absolutely.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈbaɪɪŋ kæn bɪˈkʌm ɪts oʊn dɪˈstrækʃən oʊ ˌæbsəˈlutli/

segments.text: I didn't need a beautiful painting room.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈdɪdənt nid ə ˈbjutəfəl ˈpeɪntɪŋ rum/

segments.text: I needed to move a plate, put some paper down, and find the old brushes. That's reassuring.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈnidəd tu muv ə pleɪt pʊt sʌm ˈpeɪpər daʊn ənd faɪnd ðə oʊld ˈbrʌʃɪz ðæts ˌriəˈʃʊrɪŋ/

segments.text: If I need a new chair, a special light, and a perfect room before I play guitar,
segments.ipa: /ɪf aɪ nid ə nu tʃɛr ə ˈspɛʃəl laɪt ənd ə pərˈfɛkt rum bɪˈfɔr aɪ pleɪ ɡɪˈtɑr/

segments.text: I'm giving myself several reasons to wait. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡɪvɪŋ ˌmaɪˈsɛlf ˈsɛvrəl ˈrizənz tu weɪt ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: But a shared home needs a shared plan, too.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ə ʃɛrd hoʊm nidz ə ʃɛrd plæn tu/

segments.text: My sister tells her partner when she'd like a little time to sew, and they work it out together.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər tɛlz hɝ ˈpɑrtnər wɛn ʃid laɪk ə ˈlɪtəl taɪm tu soʊ ənd ðeɪ wɝk ɪt aʊt təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: So protecting your time doesn't mean pretending other people's needs don't exist.
segments.ipa: /soʊ prəˈtɛktɪŋ jɔr taɪm ˈdʌzənt min priˈtɛndɪŋ ˈʌðər ˈpipəlz nidz doʊnt ɪɡˈzɪst/

segments.text: It means asking for room and helping them have some room as well.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈæskɪŋ fɔr rum ənd ˈhɛlpɪŋ ðɛm hæv sʌm rum æz wɛl/

segments.text: Yes, and the plan can change.
segments.ipa: /jɛs ənd ðə plæn kæn tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: If someone's sick or work runs late, missing that time doesn't mean you weren't serious about yourself.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsʌmˌwʌnz sɪk ɔr wɝk rʌnz leɪt ˈmɪsɪŋ ðæt taɪm ˈdʌzənt min ju ˈwɝənt ˈsɪriəs əˈbaʊt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: I'm glad you said that.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ɡlæd ju sɛd ðæt/

segments.text: Advice about free time sometimes sounds as if everyone has the same amount of money,
segments.ipa: /ædˈvaɪs əˈbaʊt fri taɪm səmˈtaɪmz saʊndz æz ɪf ˈɛvriˌwʌn hæz ðə seɪm əˈmaʊnt ʌv ˈmʌni/

segments.text: energy, and help at home. They don't.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛnərdʒi ənd hɛlp æt hoʊm ðeɪ doʊnt/

segments.text: And if you decide to sell something because you need the income, you haven't ruined it.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ju ˌdɪˈsaɪd tu sɛl ˈsʌmθɪŋ bɪˈkɔz ju nid ðə ˈɪnˌkʌm ju ˈhævənt ˈruənd ɪt/

segments.text: You can make that choice honestly.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn meɪk ðæt tʃɔɪs ˈɑnəstli/

segments.text: Maybe ask what the work would involve accepting orders.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi æsk wʌt ðə wɝk wʊd ˌɪnˈvɑlv ækˈsɛptɪŋ ˈɔrdərz/

segments.text: The price of the materials is one part, your time and energy are another. Right.
segments.ipa: /ðə praɪs ʌv ðə məˈtɪriəlz ɪz wʌn pɑrt jɔr taɪm ənd ˈɛnərdʒi ɑr əˈnʌðər raɪt/

segments.text: Try a small amount if you want to and notice how it feels.
segments.ipa: /traɪ ə smɔl əˈmaʊnt ɪf ju wɑnt tu ənd ˈnoʊtəs haʊ ɪt filz/

segments.text: You can keep some activities private even if you turn another one into work.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn kip sʌm ækˈtɪvətiz ˈpraɪvət ˈivɪn ɪf ju tɝn əˈnʌðər wʌn ˈɪntu wɝk/

segments.text: That makes it less like choosing one kind of life forever.
segments.ipa: /ðæt meɪks ɪt lɛs laɪk ˈtʃuzɪŋ wʌn kaɪnd ʌv laɪf fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: You can be proud of a business and still have something nobody can order from you.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn bi praʊd ʌv ə ˈbɪznəs ənd stɪl hæv ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi kæn ˈɔrdər frʌm ju/

segments.text: I like that.
segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: My sister has kept the little drawing her daughter made of that yellow pocket.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər hæz kɛpt ðə ˈlɪtəl ˈdrɔɪŋ hɝ ˈdɔtər meɪd ʌv ðæt ˈjɛloʊ ˈpɑkət/

segments.text: The pocket's enormous in the picture, bigger than the whole jacket.
segments.ipa: /ðə pocket's ɪˈnɔrməs ɪn ðə ˈpɪktʃər ˈbɪɡər ðæn ðə hoʊl ˈdʒækət/

segments.text: Clearly the important part.
segments.ipa: /ˈklɪrli ðə ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt pɑrt/

segments.text: Does your sister keep it near the sewing machine or is that too dangerous with all the scissors around?
segments.ipa: /dʌz jɔr ˈsɪstər kip ɪt nɪr ðə ˈsoʊɪŋ məˈʃin ɔr ɪz ðæt tu ˈdeɪndʒərəs wɪð ɔl ðə ˈsɪzərz ərˈaʊnd/

segments.text: It's on the fridge.
segments.ipa: /ɪts ɑn ðə frɪdʒ/

segments.text: She told me she looks at it when she's tired.
segments.ipa: /ʃi toʊld mi ʃi lʊks æt ɪt wɛn ʃiz ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: Her daughter remembers that they chose the yellow fabric together.
segments.ipa: /hɝ ˈdɔtər rɪˈmɛmbərz ðæt ðeɪ tʃoʊz ðə ˈjɛloʊ ˈfæbrɪk təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: She remembers being included.
segments.ipa: /ʃi rɪˈmɛmbərz ˈbiɪŋ ˌɪnˈkludəd/

segments.text: Your sister may have thought she was only fixing a pocket, but her daughter got a moment she wanted to draw. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈsɪstər meɪ hæv θɔt ʃi wɑz ˈoʊnli ˈfɪksɪŋ ə ˈpɑkət bʌt hɝ ˈdɔtər ɡɑt ə ˈmoʊmənt ʃi ˈwɔntɪd tu drɔ ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: We don't always get to see what our small moments mean to someone else and even when nobody else notices,
segments.ipa: /wi doʊnt ˈɔlˌweɪz ɡɛt tu si wʌt ˈaʊər smɔl ˈmoʊmənts min tu ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɛls ənd ˈivɪn wɛn ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi ɛls ˈnoʊtəsəz/

segments.text: we still get to have them.
segments.ipa: /wi stɪl ɡɛt tu hæv ðɛm/

segments.text: That last part matters.
segments.ipa: /ðæt læst pɑrt ˈmætərz/

segments.text: Someone living alone shouldn't have to find another person to make their quiet evening count.
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌmˌwʌn ˈlɪvɪŋ əˈloʊn ˈʃʊdənt hæv tu faɪnd əˈnʌðər ˈpɝsən tu meɪk ðɛr ˈkwaɪət ˈivnɪŋ kaʊnt/

segments.text: Enjoying it can be enough. It can.
segments.ipa: /ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪɪŋ ɪt kæn bi ɪˈnʌf ɪt kæn/

segments.text: You might be 28 and building a career, 40 and caring for a family,
segments.ipa: /ju maɪt bi ənd ˈbɪldɪŋ ə kərˈɪr ənd ˈkɛrɪŋ fɔr ə ˈfæməli/

segments.text: or 60 and finding a different rhythm.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ənd ˈfaɪndɪŋ ə ˈdɪfərənt ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: You're allowed to have an interest.
segments.ipa: /jʊr əˈlaʊd tu hæv æn ˈɪntrəst/

segments.text: And you're allowed to be an ordinary person doing it.
segments.ipa: /ənd jʊr əˈlaʊd tu bi æn ˈɔrdəˌnɛri ˈpɝsən ˈduɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: An ordinary voice singing in a kitchen can belong to a very good evening.
segments.ipa: /æn ˈɔrdəˌnɛri vɔɪs ˈsɪŋɪŋ ɪn ə ˈkɪtʃən kæn bɪˈlɔŋ tu ə ˈvɛri ɡʊd ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: That's the feeling I hope people keep.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ðə ˈfilɪŋ aɪ hoʊp ˈpipəl kip/

segments.text: The day already asks so much from you.
segments.ipa: /ðə deɪ ɔlˈrɛdi æsks soʊ mʌtʃ frʌm ju/

segments.text: A hobby can be a place where you don't have to prove anything.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhɑbi kæn bi ə pleɪs wɛr ju doʊnt hæv tu pruv ˈɛniˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: I'm going to leave my guitar where I can see it tonight.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu liv maɪ ɡɪˈtɑr wɛr aɪ kæn si ɪt təˈnaɪt/

segments.text: Then I'll ask my dad for a song.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪl æsk maɪ dæd fɔr ə sɔŋ/

segments.text: Have you decided where the painting goes?
segments.ipa: /hæv ju ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪd wɛr ðə ˈpeɪntɪŋ ɡoʊz/

segments.text: On the kitchen wall beside the window I tried to paint.
segments.ipa: /ɑn ðə ˈkɪtʃən wɔl bɪˈsaɪd ðə ˈwɪndoʊ aɪ traɪd tu peɪnt/

segments.text: If anyone thinks it's a bus stop, I'll offer them a seat.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈɛniˌwʌn θɪŋks ɪts ə bʌs stɑp aɪl ˈɔfər ðɛm ə sit/

segments.text: I'd visit that bus stop, and I'd bring a loaf of bread, provided nobody asks me to deliver 20 more before breakfast.
segments.ipa: /aɪd ˈvɪzɪt ðæt bʌs stɑp ənd aɪd brɪŋ ə loʊf ʌv brɛd prəˈvaɪdɪd ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi æsks mi tu dɪˈlɪvər mɔr bɪˈfɔr ˈbrɛkfəst/

segments.text: One loaf sounds perfect.
segments.ipa: /wʌn loʊf saʊndz pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: And to everyone listening, thanks for spending this time with us and practicing your English through a real conversation.
segments.ipa: /ənd tu ˈɛvriˌwʌn ˈlɪsənɪŋ θæŋks fɔr ˈspɛndɪŋ ðɪs taɪm wɪð ʌs ənd ˈpræktəsɪŋ jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ θru ə ril ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən/

segments.text: We hope you found a phrase you can use and an idea you want to try.
segments.ipa: /wi hoʊp ju faʊnd ə freɪz ju kæn jus ənd æn aɪˈdiə ju wɑnt tu traɪ/

segments.text: We'd love to hear what you do for fun.
segments.ipa: /wid lʌv tu hir wʌt ju du fɔr fʌn/

segments.text: Thanks for listening to Mr. English channel.
segments.ipa: /θæŋks fɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu ˈmɪstər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl/

segments.text: Keep practicing, take care of yourself, and we'll see you in the next episode. Goodbye, everyone. Goodbye.
segments.ipa: /kip ˈpræktəsɪŋ teɪk kɛr ʌv jərˈsɛlf ənd wil si ju ɪn ðə nɛkst ˈɛpəˌsoʊd ˌɡʊdˈbaɪ ˈɛvriˌwʌn ˌɡʊdˈbaɪ/
